narration: The whole pipeline sits behind a thin translucent layer. We start on the left, where the incoming LiDAR scan P t enters the loop, and the orange return path that will later feed back the next scan, P t plus one.
The first stage comes into focus: geometry-aware point sampling. Instead of using every point in the scan, this block picks a small, well-spread subset to work with.
Inside it, eigen feature computation runs first. For each point it analyses the local neighbourhood and derives eigenvalue-based descriptors of the surrounding geometry.
Those descriptors pass through a threshold, which keeps only the points lying on geometrically salient structure and discards flat, uninformative regions.
Random sampling then thins the surviving points down to a fixed, manageable budget, so the cost of the later stages stays bounded.
The sampled points travel along the orange arrow into the second stage, view-based partitioning.

Partitioning is driven by the azimuthal angle of each point around the sensor. The diagram shows the vehicle at the centre, with the surrounding space cut into front, rear, left-side and right-side sectors.
That gives four separate point sets: front view, left view, right view and rear view. Splitting the scan this way keeps matching local and avoids mixing points from opposite directions.
The four view sets run down the right-hand loop into the third stage, feature extraction and matching.
Features are produced by PointHop plus plus, a feed-forward, successive-subspace module that builds a compact descriptor for every point without any back-propagation training.
Feature matching is then performed independently in each view, pairing points of the current scan with points of the previous one to form the correspondences.
Those correspondences flow left into the final stage, motion estimation and update.
From the matched pairs the system estimates the rotation and translation between the two consecutive scans, which is the frame-to-frame motion of the sensor.
That relative pose is accumulated to update the trajectory, extending the estimated path travelled so far.
Finally the time index is advanced, t becomes t plus one, and control returns along the orange loop so the next scan enters the pipeline as the new P t.

The mask lifts completely: geometry-aware sampling, view-based partitioning, PointHop plus plus feature extraction and matching, and motion estimation form one closed odometry loop that runs once per incoming scan.
